claim: In the Bala-Goyal bandit model with a nearly indistinguishable better arm (0.501 vs 0.5), sparse networks (cycle) learn the better action more reliably than denser ones (wheel, complete), at sizes 3-12.
agent_test: Simulate a Bala-Goyal bandit with k LLM agents on cycle vs complete graph on a hard, noisy 2-option task at equal total tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The cost of sparsity is speed: the complete graph converges fastest, the cycle slowest (size 100: about 20 vs about 1,977 rounds).
agent_test: Count rounds and tokens to correct consensus per topology; report accuracy per token, not per round.
audit_note: Size-100 figures hold at pB=0.501, n=1000; Rosenstock et al. extend Zollman's model but are different authors.

claim: The Zollman effect is parameter-fragile: it vanishes when the better arm is easy to detect (gap 0 for pB>=0.525; under 2 points at 0.51), and is largest with few agents and few trials per round. It never reversed in their sweep. Both evidence streams trace to one paper (Rosenstock et al 2017), so true independence is 1; it could not be re-opened in the cross-check.
agent_test: Scale task hardness (signal gap) and check whether the isolation advantage shrinks on easy items.

claim: Reversal exists: with epsilon-greedy exploratory agents (eps=0.35) complete networks beat cycles (Kummerfeld and Zollman 2016); this also shrinks under wider payoff parameters.
agent_test: Vary agent exploration rate (temperature) with topology; expect isolation to help low-exploration agents and hurt high-exploration ones.

claim: Density, not hub centrality, predicts failure: degree variance is uncorrelated with success across all graphs of size 3-6, and the cycle beats the wheel.
agent_test: Compare hub-and-spoke (one aggregator reading all) vs ring vs complete at equal budget.

claim: Mechanism is containment: after bad luck, about 4x more agents switch strategy in dense networks, so diversity of action is lost early.
agent_test: Measure answer diversity (pairwise distance) after round 1 across topologies; relate it to final accuracy.

claim: Which topology wins on rugged landscapes depends on the copying rule: best-member copying favors slow networks (diameter vs payoff r=+0.83), conformity favors fast networks (r=-0.77). This reconciles Lazer-Friedman and Mason-Watts, but only in simulation.
agent_test: Test revision rule: copy-best-scored vs follow-majority, with sparse vs dense sharing, on a search task with a verifier.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Conformity pressure in network models raises wrong consensus and polarisation: at k=0.1 only about 16% of runs reach any consensus; correct 55%, incorrect 44% (k=0: 96% true consensus). Verified against paper text.
agent_test: Add a no-peer-answer-visible condition; measure flips from correct to wrong.

claim: Human experiments do not give a clean replication of the Zollman effect. Mason and Watts (256 web experiments, groups of 16) found efficient networks did better (beta -4.63, P about 0.01) and networked groups beat independent ones (68 vs 39 points when the peak was found). Derex and Boyd (12 groups of 6 per arm) found temporary isolation helped: both third-level innovations 58.3% vs 0%. The two differ in task (smooth search map vs recombination puzzle) and in isolation (none vs first 36 trials only). Primary papers now opened.
agent_test: Treat as a weak prior: isolate first, merge later, only when solutions can be recombined or checked; test directly on the agent.

claim: Sparse or reduced LLM debate matches or beats fully connected debate at far lower cost: neighbour-connected about +2% on MATH, input tokens down 41.5-43.5%; random 10-30% edge pruning gained up to 2.83% on MMLU. Li 2024 figures verified.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison: full visibility vs 2-neighbour visibility in revision rounds.

claim: Debate gains are largely explained by voting over independent answers; debate is a martingale in expectation, and majority vote is on par with debate in most cases.
agent_test: Always include independent samples plus vote at equal tokens as the baseline; adopt debate only if it beats it.
audit_note: Debate or Vote says majority voting accounts for 'most' of MAD's gains and the martingale result is theoretical; Stop Overvaluing independently finds MAD rarely beats CoT/SC.

claim: Communication can reduce accuracy: correct-to-wrong flips are highest when an agent is alone in its answer; a lone correct agent facing a wrong majority recovers only 3.6-34.4% of the time.
agent_test: Count correct-to-wrong flips after exposure to peer answers, compared with no-exposure resampling.
audit_note: Minor: 3.6-34.4% covers three models in one study (Wu et al.), not all LLMs.

claim: Full-solution interaction homogenises agents (pairwise distance 0.315 to 0.229 in one round) and hurts diverse teams (Debate -0.078 vs +0.012 same-model); only independent-proposer MoA stays positive. Verified against paper text; the diversity effect disappears without one task (+0.014).
agent_test: Measure diversity before and after any sharing step; prefer independent proposers plus a selector.

claim: Dense graphs spread a planted error more; sparse graphs pass a planted correct insight less (error spread cut up to 19% Full to Chain; correct uptake up 10.5% Chain to Full). Best accuracy at moderate sparsity.
agent_test: Plant a wrong or right sketch in one attempt and measure spread under different visibility.

claim: Dense is not always worse for LLM networks: Han 2026 found denser graphs converge faster and slightly more accurate (specific 0.70 vs 0.75 not verified) while risking wrong-but-sure cascades; Zheng 2026 finds LLMs need more links than theory because they under-report negative results (35-53% Qwen, 69-84% GPT). New: with every verdict (including failures) sent automatically the agents approach theory; the excess critical degree under free communication correlates r = -0.91 with the report rate. Token cost of forced sharing not measured.
agent_test: Force explicit reporting of failed attempts into the shared channel and test.

claim: Topology rank is task-dependent in LLM agent graphs: no topology wins everywhere; irregular random topologies often beat dense mesh; random fresh-peer routing is a strong baseline over learned topology.
agent_test: Do not tune topology; default to random few-peer visibility or none.

claim: Heterogeneity (different models) helps debate and ensembles but hurts naive full-solution interaction; a strong model at a hub helps a little.
agent_test: Vary prompt or persona diversity across attempts vs same prompt at equal tokens.

claim: Teams under-use experts and fall below their best member (HLE: best individual 29.0%, team 28.0%, expert revealed 36.0%; relative synergy gap 6.3-41.1%). Pappu figures verified.
agent_test: Prefer selection by verifier or confidence over averaging views.

claim: Independent sampling plus voting scales without communication, with larger gains on harder tasks (GSM8K +12 to +24, MATH +6 to +10), and plateaus near 8 agents in MacNet.
agent_test: Scale N independent attempts to the budget and run a plateau test.
audit_note: Minor: Li et al. report the larger gain with task difficulty as relative gain within and across GSM8K/MATH, while the quoted absolute ranges (GSM8K bigger than MATH) do not themselves show it.

claim: At matched thinking tokens a single agent equals or beats multi-agent setups beyond very small budgets (100 tokens: single 0.290 vs debate 0.370; 500 tokens: 0.390 vs 0.380). Verified against paper table.
agent_test: Always compare against one long single attempt at equal tokens.

claim: Higher reasoning effort and low temperature make LLM agents herd, so more links are needed for the same benefit; ring topology stays fragmented while rewired graphs synchronise. New: unique literals tested fell 25.5 to 11.3 (TCAS) and 14.2 to 8.8 (physics) with higher effort; temperature 0.2 mattered mostly where the clue is obvious; independent samples are highly similar even at temperature 2.0 with min-p (81% of pairs above 0.7 similarity, open-ended tasks).
agent_test: Vary temperature and effort and measure answer diversity across independent attempts.

claim: Chain topologies accumulate error most (amplification chain 2094 vs mesh 1241 vs star 1184; 100 trials, Qwen2.5-7B); sequential refinement passes errors on.
agent_test: Compare sequential revision (chain) against parallel attempts then aggregate.

claim: Multi-agent systems often fail through inter-agent misalignment (MAST: 14 failure modes, annotator kappa 0.88).
agent_test: Audit agent traces for the most frequent modes.

claim: In a human cumulative-innovation task, temporary isolation (first 36 of 72 trials) then contact let partial groups combine two innovation lines (58.3% vs 0% of groups), at the cost of a slower short run. The isolate-then-merge pattern is the useful part, not permanent isolation.
agent_test: Run independent attempts, then one merge step; compare with a shared-from-start arm at equal tokens.

claim: Bala and Goyal show in theory that a small publicly seen group (Royal Family of 5) can lock a society into the worse action with probability up to about 0.2 in simulation (N=100); extra links can make a society worse off.
agent_test: Test whether a shared first answer (hub) pulls later attempts off the better path.

claim: A single LLM in a bandit fails to explore without outside help: GPT-4 basic prompt shows suffix failures in more than 60% of replicates (K=5, gap 0.2, T=100 to 200); only one of the tested configurations (chain-of-thought plus externally summarised history) worked. No study yet compares independent vs shared LLM agents on a real bandit.
agent_test: Run N independent restarts versus one long run on a small bandit or a hidden-rule task at equal tokens.

claim: Task difficulty decides whether revising or fresh sampling is better: on easy MATH questions sequential revision wins; on hard ones independent parallel samples (or a mix) win; a tuned reviser and a verifier are involved. Evidence is from a single paper with a fine-tuned reviser.
agent_test: Route by first-sample agreement: high agreement means revise once; low agreement means fresh independent attempts.

claim: Without a real external check, revising one's own answer is no better than fresh samples at equal budget: code self-repair gives marginal or no gains vs more initial samples; intrinsic reasoning self-correction lowered accuracy (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1). Contrary hint: refinement beat one long chain at matched sequential tokens (76.9 to 81.5 to 86.7), but that is not a fresh-sample comparison.
agent_test: Compare fresh-attempt vote vs one revision round at equal total tokens by task type; use revision only with an external check.

claim: Revision or merge steps are exposed to anchoring: admitting wrong candidates into a bounded workspace caused large accuracy drops (AIME 2024, o3-mini, gemini-2.5-flash), larger for the weaker self-verifier.
agent_test: Check whether a merge step sees only checked or deduplicated candidates.

claim: Independent multi-agent runs without a check amplify errors (17.2x vs 4.4x with a central validator) and hurt where a single agent already exceeds about 45% (beta -0.236, p=0.004); BrowseComp-Plus -35%, PlanCraft up to -70% for independent runs.
agent_test: Never aggregate independent attempts without a validator or vote; skip extra attempts on easy items.

claim: Plain majority vote and reward-model selection plateau (MATH, Llama-3-8B: 40.50% to 41.41% from 100 to 10,000 samples) while coverage rises 82.9% to 98.44%; a real verifier is needed to convert extra attempts into accuracy. Confidence-weighted voting (CISC) cuts the needed samples by about 41% at a budget of 5 and 46% at 10.
agent_test: Use verifier when one exists; else confidence-weighted vote. Measure plateau on our own tasks.

claim: Hard-signal tasks favour independence more than easy ones: supported indirectly (Rosenstock model, Snell difficulty split, Olausson, Kim capability ceiling, Zheng obvious-clue exception) but no LLM study varied the signal gap directly.
agent_test: Vary item difficulty on one benchmark and compare independent vs shared at equal tokens.
